The first Air Jordan shoe was released in 1985, designed by Peter Moore. The shoe featured a bold red and black colorway, which was banned by the NBA as they did not conform to the league’s uniform policy. Michael Jordan was fined $5,000 every time he wore them on the court, but this only served to boost the shoe’s popularity. The Air Jordan 1 was an instant hit and sold out quickly.
Following the success of the first Air Jordan shoe, Nike released new designs every year, each one with its own unique features and design elements. Some of the most popular and iconic designs include the Air Jordan 3, 4, 5, 6, and 11. Each shoe had its own backstory and design inspiration, but all of them were made with performance in mind and were worn by Michael Jordan during his time in the NBA.

One of the most notable collaborations was with designer Virgil Abloh’s Off-White label in 2017, which featured a reworked version of the Air Jordan 1.
The Air Jordan brand has also had a significant impact on popular culture. Many people collect and wear the shoes as a fashion statement, and the brand has been featured in numerous films, television shows, and music videos. The brand has also been referenced in countless songs and has been worn by many celebrities.
In conclusion, the Air Jordan brand has had a significant impact on both basketball and fashion. From its humble beginnings in 1985 to its current status as a cultural phenomenon, the brand has remained relevant and beloved by fans all over the world.
